rationale: Enumerative cosmological term used throughout the page: 'first kind,' 'fourth kind,' 'twelve kinds.' Likely Lycopolitan reflex of ⲧⲱϣ/ⲧⲱⲉ 'division, tribe' with ⲱ→ⲁ shift, or a related categorial noun. The chapter heading at line 31-32 ('mystery of the twelve kinds that came to be in the darkness') makes this a key technical term for the dark-cosmological taxonomy parallel to the twelve zodiac-signs.

Found paired with ⲧⲁⲓ̈ⲉ in line 21: 'ⲧⲙⲏⲧⲉ ⲛ̄ⲧⲁⲓ̈ⲉ ⲧϯⲉ ⲛⲧⲁⲓ̈ⲉ ⲍⲁⲩⲧ ⲙⲛ̄ ⲧϯⲉ ⲛⲛⲉⲥⲍⲁⲙⲉ' — 'the middle of the kinds, the ⲧϯⲉ of male kinds with the ⲧϯⲉ of females.' Distinct from ϯⲟⲩ 'five' (consistently spelled ⲡϯⲟⲩ on this page) and from ϯⲡⲉ 'taste/kind.' Tentatively rendered 'portion' as the gender-half of each kind.

Greek-derived verb τάσσω with 3sg masculine suffix ϩ (= Sah. ϥ): ⲁⲩⲧⲁⲭⲁϩ ϣⲁⲁⲛⲏⲍⲉ 'they fixed him for ever' (l.31). Cf. accumulated vocabulary entry ⲧⲁⲝⲟ/ⲧⲁⲝⲣⲟ 'appoint, establish.' Lycopolitan ⲭ for ξ. Eschatological/cosmological binding sense.

Lycopolitan reflex of Sahidic ⲥⲁⲛⲟⲩϣ 'nourish, feed, rear.' Used in line 25 of those who 'nourished the five elements' — possibly the cosmic guardian-powers that sustain the dark elements within their kinds.

Lycopolitan reflex of Sahidic ⲥⲱⲣ 'spread, scatter' with directional ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'forth.' Cosmogonic verb appearing twice on this page: line 17 ⲁⲥⲥⲁⲣⲥ̄ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'she spread forth (to her offspring)' and line 20-21 ⲁ(ⲥ)ⲥⲁⲣϩ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'spread forth (into the middle of the kinds).' Describes the propagation of darkness through its emanations.
